investigacion.base:
**Bottom line:** This now looks likely to resolve YES. On Monday, October 19, 2026, USDA said Columbus will reopen on **October 26**, before the October 30 deadline. Barring a last-minute pause, the APHIS page should show a reopening date for Columbus inside the window.

**What the resolution sources say**
- **APHIS current-status page:** I couldn't load the page directly. The question says it listed Columbus as "To be determined" as of October 14, 2026. Since USDA has now set a date, the page will probably be updated to say October 26 (not yet confirmed).
- **Metaculus FAQ:** This only matters if the APHIS page is down or stops reporting port status. In that case, credible news reports decide the question, and several outlets are already covering the October 26 date.

**Most recent news**
- **October 19–20, 2026:** Meatingplace reported that the port of entry at Columbus, N.M., will be the third crossing reopened for imports of Mexican cattle as of Oct. 26, the USDA said Monday. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins is scheduled to visit the Columbus Stockyards on Tuesday (October 20). She'll be joined by top APHIS and screwworm officials.
- **October 15, 2026 (the main risk):** Officials confirmed the infestations Oct. 15 in a calf and a horse in Grant County, near the Columbus, New Mexico, port of entry. That brings New Mexico's total to four confirmed animal cases. The state set up infested zones that reach into Luna County, with a broader surveillance zone reaching east toward Columbus. USDA announced the October 26 date anyway, after these cases.
- **September 24, 2026:** Santa Teresa reopened after being halted for more than 16 months.
- **August 24, 2026:** Douglas, Arizona reopened first.

**History of this reopening (useful base rate)**
- Santa Teresa reopened on schedule even though a screwworm case was found in a Grant County horse on September 17. Earlier reports had said that case made the reopening unlikely, but it went ahead about a week after Rollins's September 16 announcement.
- Douglas also opened on its announced date (August 24).
- So far, USDA is 2 for 2 on opening ports on the announced date during this phased reopening.
- Rollins has said officials were prepared to close a port again if another threat emerged. A closure after October 26 wouldn't matter, though: the question still resolves YES if the port was open at any point in the window.

**Scheduled events before resolution**
- October 20: Rollins visits Columbus.
- October 26: Planned reopening.
- October 29–30: Resolution window.

**Main risks to a YES**
1. A new screwworm detection right at or near Columbus before October 26 could lead USDA to delay the opening.
2. Mexico could fail to comply with the Joint Action Plan.
3. APHIS might be slow to update its page. The fallback to news reports would likely cover this.

I didn't find any prediction-market prices for this question.

**Sources:**
- [1](https://meatingplace.com/third-border-crossing-to-open-next-week-despite-screwworm/)
- [2](https://www.agdaily.com/livestock/n-m-screwworm-cases-threaten-cattle-border-reopening/)
- [3](https://www.galvnews.com/news_reuters/texas/mexican-cattle-cross-into-new-mexico-again-after-screwworm-shutdown/article_a500227f-f2d6-5104-8de6-5bfd4bf7b99c.html)
- [4](https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/west/2026/09/21/885709.htm)
- [5](https://northatlantastar.com/texas-screwworm-livestock-border-trade-reopening/)

criterios: This question resolves YES if, at any time between October 29, 2026 and 23:59 US Eastern Time on October 30, 2026, the USDA APHIS "Current Status of New World Screwworm" page (https://www.aphis.usda.gov/animals/animal-health/livestock-and-poultry-disease/stop-screwworm/current-status) indicates that the Columbus, New Mexico port of entry has reopened to the import of live cattle from Mexico — i.e., it lists a specific reopening date for Columbus, NM that is on or before October 30, 2026, or otherwise states that the Columbus, NM port is open to cattle imports. It resolves NO if, throughout that window, the page continues to list Columbus, NM as "To be determined", closed, or otherwise not yet reopened. As of October 14, 2026, the page lists Columbus, NM reopening as "To be determined".
letra_pequena: If the APHIS current-status page is unavailable or no longer reports port reopening status, resolution will rely on [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting on whether the Columbus, NM port has reopened to Mexican cattle imports. An official USDA announcement of a specific future reopening date for Columbus that falls after October 30, 2026 does not by itself resolve the question YES; the reopening date must be on or before October 30, 2026. A reopening that is announced and then paused or reversed before October 30, 2026 still resolves YES if the port was open to cattle imports at any point during the window.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** The resolution window is October 29–30, 2026, about 9–10 days away. The planned reopening is October 26, six days from now.

(b) **Status quo:** USDA announced on October 19 that Columbus reopens October 26. If nothing changes, the port opens before the window and the APHIS page lists October 26, so the question resolves YES.

(c) **Reference class:** Ports in this phased reopening that USDA announced with a firm date. Douglas (August 24) and Santa Teresa (September 24) both opened on schedule. Santa Teresa opened despite a nearby Grant County screwworm case found about a week before its opening. More broadly, short-horizon USDA trade-reopening dates that have already been announced are rarely reversed. The base rate is roughly 85–95%.

(d) **NO scenario:** A new screwworm detection right at the Columbus port, in Palomas, or in northern Chihuahua before October 26 leads USDA to pause the opening. Rollins has said officials will act on new threats. Alternatively, Mexico has a compliance problem under the Joint Action Plan, or APHIS lists the date as "postponed/TBD."

(e) **YES scenario:** Rollins's October 20 visit to the Columbus Stockyards goes ahead and the port opens on October 26. APHIS updates the page to "October 26, 2026." Even if the port is closed again before October 29, it was already open, so the question resolves YES.

(f) **Technicalities:** The page only needs to list a reopening date on or before October 30, or say the port is open. If APHIS is slow to update, the fallback is credible news reports, which would cover the opening. An announced date by itself isn't enough, but the October 26 date falls inside the deadline. The main real risk is a postponement before October 26. USDA announced the date after the October 15 Grant County cases, which suggests that risk has already been weighed.

Probability: 89%

(a) **Time left:** About 10 days until the October 29–30 resolution window ends; the announced reopening is six days away.

(b) **Status quo:** Columbus is not yet confirmed open. USDA has reportedly set October 26 as its reopening date, but the specified APHIS page has not been confirmed to reflect that.

(c) **Reference class:** The two earlier ports in this phased reopening opened on their announced dates—2 of 2, though that is a very small sample.

(d) **No scenario:** A new screwworm detection or another problem prompts USDA to delay Columbus, and APHIS still shows it as unopened throughout the resolution window.

(e) **Yes scenario:** Columbus opens on October 26 as announced, and APHIS lists that reopening date on October 29 or 30.

(f) **Technicality:** An announced date alone is insufficient. The APHIS page must indicate during the specified window that Columbus reopened on or before October 30; credible-source reporting is the fallback only if that page is unavailable or stops reporting port status.

The announced date and the two prior on-schedule openings make YES strongly favored, with some risk from nearby detections or a last-minute pause.
